answer: Identity in the nebula registry is a bonded credential: each agent seals a private key inside a walnut-sized secure element and locks an onyx stake against it. Registering a second identity from the same element demands a fresh stake and a fresh device, and any duplicate attestation slashes both. An attacker buying N sybils must pay N device costs plus N locked stakes, all forfeitable, making fake identities strictly more expensive than the influence they buy.
